airport.name: Rio Galeão – Tom Jobim International Airport

summary: Rio Galeão – Tom Jobim International Airport (GIG) is Brazil's principal gateway to Rio de Janeiro, situated on Governador Island in Guanabara Bay about 20 km from the city center. Officially renamed in 1999 to honor the legendary bossa nova composer Antônio Carlos Jobim, it features two modern terminals originally built and expanded for the 2016 Olympic Games. The airport handles the majority of Rio's international traffic and serves as a major hub for both domestic carriers and intercontinental flights.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from central Rio de Janeiro?
A: GIG is located on Governador Island, roughly 20 km (12 miles) from downtown Rio and about 30 km from the famous Copacabana and Ipanema beaches, with typical travel times of 30–60 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Why is the airport named after Tom Jobim?
A: The airport was renamed in 1999 to honor Antônio Carlos 'Tom' Jobim, the iconic Brazilian composer and singer who helped create bossa nova music. His name reflects Rio's deep cultural heritage.

Q: How many terminals does GIG have?
A: The airport operates two main terminals: Terminal 1 handles most domestic flights, while Terminal 2 serves international departures and arrivals, both connected by shuttle buses and integrated walkways.

Q: Is there free Wi-Fi available at the airport?
A: Yes, complimentary Wi-Fi is offered throughout both terminals, though speed and reliability may vary during peak travel periods.
transport_tips: The Galeão light rail station is not yet operational for direct city center access, so most travelers rely on taxis, app-based rideshares (Uber and 99), or pre-booked airport transfers.
